title: What is the P2 distance?
text: Welfare, development living standards multidimensional concepts. single variable (income, GDP, etc.) fully captures , combining many indicators one synthetic measure raises hard question: aggregate variables expressed different units , , avoid double-counting information several correlated indicators share? P_2 distance (Pena, 1977) designed solve exactly problem. distance-based synthetic indicator: instead choosing arbitrary weights variable, measures far unit analysis (region, municipality, household…) lies reference situation, corrects measure indicators carrying redundant (correlated) information counted twice. Bonet-García et al. (2015) used p2distance package build indicator human well-Andalusian municipalities, good worked illustration method described .

what: How the P2 distance is computed
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: p2distance() function implements algorithm described Bonet-García et al. (2015) (following Pena (1977), Montero et al. (2010)). explanation follows notation paper.

previous_headings: How the P2 distance is computed
what: 1. The data matrix and the reference vector
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: starting point matrix X order (m, n), m number spatial (statistical) units (e.g. municipalities, countries, households) n number variables (indicators). element x_{ri} value variable unit r. measure far unit ideal reference situation, reference vector X_* = (x_{*1}, x_{*2}, \ldots, x_{*n}) must defined: one reference value per variable. vector represents condition units compared can used (minimum, maximum, average, user-defined target, etc.). minimum value often used sociological studies (Rodríguez Martín, 2011; Somarriba & Pena, 2009; Zarzosa & Somarriba, 2012), default used makeReferenceVector(); vector reflects ideal condition units compared can also used.

previous_headings: How the P2 distance is computed
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: every variable, distance unit reference value calculated: d_{ri} = |x_{ri} - x_{*}|, \qquad r = 1, \ldots, m; \; = 1, \ldots, n \qquad (\text{Eq. 1}) absolute value used positive negative deviations reference treated way (Somarriba et al., 2014). variables measured different units, partial distance standardized dividing standard deviation variable, \sigma_i, giving d_{ri}/\sigma_i.

previous_headings: How the P2 distance is computed
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: Summing standardized partial distances across variables gives Fréchet Distance: FD(r) = \sum_{=1}^{n} \frac{d_{ri}}{\sigma_i} = \sum_{=1}^{n} \frac{|x_{ri}-x_{*}|}{\sigma_i}, \qquad r = 1, \ldots, m \qquad (\text{Eq. 2}) FD(r) maximum value P_2 distance can reach unit r. FD concept distance valid theoretical situation uncorrelated indicators. However, common find direct relationships partial indicators, implies FD includes duplicate information.

previous_headings: How the P2 distance is computed
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: remove redundancy, partial indicator weighted correction factor (1 - R^2_{,-1,\ldots,1}), R^2_{,-1,\ldots,1} coefficient determination linear regression indicator indicators already entered index (-1, -2, \ldots, 1). coefficient measures proportion variance indicator already explained (linearly dependent ) indicators already included. factor (1 - R^2) therefore keeps genuinely new information indicator contributes discards redundant indicators (Pena, 1977). indicators mutually uncorrelated, every R^2 = 0 P_2 distance simply equals FD.

previous_headings: How the P2 distance is computed
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: Applying correction factor every term sum gives P_2 distance: P_2(r) = \sum_{=1}^{n} \left\{ \left(\frac{d_{ri}}{\sigma_i}\right)\left(1 - R^2_{,-1,-2,\ldots,1}\right) \right\}, \qquad r = 1, \ldots, m \qquad (\text{Eq. 3})

what: 6. Ordering the variables, and iterating to convergence
title: What is the P2 distance?
text: equation P_2 depends order variables enter index: regression used correction factor variable always variables came . Deciding order arbitrary: p2distance() uses iterative procedure Montero et al. (2010) find : Compute partial indicators d_{ri}/\sigma_i data matrix reference vector (Eq. 1). Compute Fréchet Distance FD(r) every unit (Eq. 2). Determine order entrance variables: since FD already summarizes information partial indicators, variable strongly correlated FD one contributes variance index, enters first. correlation every partial indicator FD ranks remaining variables first pass. Compute correction factors (1-R^2) variable, following order. Compute first P_2 distance, P_2^{1}, applying Eq. 3 order correction factors steps 3–4. Check convergence: correlation every variable new P_2^{1} index used re-rank order entrance, whole procedure (steps 3–5) repeated obtain P_2^{2}, P_2^{3}, . algorithm stops soon two consecutive iterations agree — .e. first P_2^{j} P_2^{j} = P_2^{j+1} final P_2 distance returned every unit. following figure summarizes procedure: (1) partial indicators computed initial data matrix using reference vector; (2) Fréchet Distance computed; (3) order entrance variables determined correlation partial indicators FD; (4) matrix reordered, correction factor variable obtained; (5) first P_2 distance, P_2^{1}, computed applying Eq. (3); (6) difference P_2^{j} P_2^{j-1} evaluated (initial iteration, FD P_2^{1} compared) — difference zero, algorithm stops; otherwise, matrix reordered according correlation partial indicators last P_2^{j} obtained, new P_2 computed.

title: What is the P2 distance?
text: Bonet-García et al. (2015) applied method compare human well-Andalusian municipalities (southern Spain) 1989 2009, combining 22 socioeconomic indicators (population, health, employment, income, infrastructure, education, culture social participation) single P_2 well-index. Well-increased significantly two years, increase significantly larger municipalities located within Natural National Parks unprotected ones (well-ratio 1.144 vs. 1.121, p = 0.0066), evidence, according authors, spatial association long-term protected-area management improvements local human well-. See full paper complete indicator list, methodology results.

title: Welfare's Synthetic Indicator
text: p2distance computes P2 distance synthetic indicator (Pena, 1977), method combining several partial indicators (quality life, welfare, environmental quality, development) single measure lets compare different entities (countries, regions, cities…) common scale. Unlike Principal Component Analysis traditional aggregation methods, P2 avoids arbitrary weighting: variable weighted much new information contributes variables already included accounted , using iterative correction based variable’s coefficient determination (R²).

text: list following elements: discrimination.coefficient: Vector discrimination coefficients (DC) variable (Ivanovic, 1974). See Zarzosa (1996) Zarzosa & Somarriba (2012). p2distance: Vector final \(P_2\) distance value spatial entity. p2distances: Matrix \(P_2\) distance values resulting iteration. diff_p2distances: Matrix differences two consecutive \(P_2\) distances. iteration: Number iterations performed. umbral: Threshold used stop iterations. variables_sort: Variable names ordered entrance order last iteration. correction_factors: Correction factor variable. cor.coeff: Correlation coefficient variable calculated \(P_2\) distance. partial.Indicators: spatial entity, difference reference vector value variable, divided standard deviation. sum partial indicators spatial entity Frechet Distance (DF), maximum value \(P_2\) distance can reach.

title: Welfare's synthetic indicator (P2 distance) — p2distance
text: \(P_2\) distance, also called DP2, used measure welfare quality--life applications, build environmental quality indexes, generally aggregate multiple partial indicators (variables) single measure allows spatial entities compared. spatial entity r, \(P_2\) distance defined : $$DP_{2}=\sum^{n}_{=1}\left\lbrace\left(\frac{d_{}}{\sigma_{}}\right)\left(1-R^{2}_{,-1,-2,\ldots,1}\right)\right\rbrace$$ \(R^{2}_{1}=0\), \(d_{}=|x_{ri}-x_{*}|\), reference base \(X_{*}=(x_{*1},x_{*2},\ldots,x_{*n})\), : n number variables \(x_{ri}\) value variable spatial entity r \(\sigma_{}\) standard deviation variable \(R^{2}_{,-1,\ldots,1}\) coefficient determination regression \(X_i\) \(X_{-1}, X_{-2}, \ldots, X_1\) already included numerical value DP2 index meaning , useful comparing state different spatial entities terms welfare, environmental conditions, etc.
